::: {#sec-srr-convention}

For the **1-stock hypothesis**, the B~MSY~ target is **6.869 million tonnes (Mt)**, based on the **long-term stock–recruitment relationship (SRR)** fitted over 2000–2023 in the base assessment. Following the assessment convention, projections use a **precautionary level of recruitment productivity**, fitted over 2001–2015, to evaluate future biomass and catch. The corresponding B~MSY~ estimate for the precautionary run is **6.041 Mt**. Both estimates use the 2017–2026 mean of annual equilibrium reference points, providing a comparison on the same averaging basis. **Projected biomass is assessed against the long-term target of 6.869 Mt.**

![1-stock hypothesis, Model 1.06: the long-term SRR supplies the BMSY target of 6.869 Mt; the precautionary SRR supplies biomass and catch projections. Its comparable BMSY estimate is 6.041 Mt, while projection risk is evaluated against the 6.869 Mt target. Both BMSY values are 2017–2026 means of annual equilibrium spawning biomass.](srr-convention-diagram.png){#fig-srr-convention width=6.4in fig-alt="1-stock hypothesis. The base SRR, fitted over 2000–2023, supplies the long-term BMSY target of 6.869 million tonnes. The precautionary SRR, fitted over 2001–2015, has a comparable BMSY estimate of 6.041 million tonnes and supplies biomass and catch projections. Projected biomass is compared with the 6.869-million-tonne long-term target. Both BMSY estimates are 2017–2026 means of annual equilibrium spawning biomass; both SRRs use steepness 0.65."}

The estimates come from the saved `h1_1.06` and `h1_1.06.ls` annual reference-point outputs (`msy_mt`). The 6.041 Mt estimate describes the precautionary run's equilibrium productivity; the annex retains 6.869 Mt as the target for stock status and the saved 11 September projection probabilities. The annual 2026 values and the separate scalar MSY calculation used to set the F~MSY~ projection scenario are distinguished in @sec-reference-diagram. Both SRRs use steepness $h = 0.65$. This carries forward the conservative recruitment convention described in the SC13 technical annex [@sprfmo2025annex, para. 84] and the SC14 working assessment [@assessment2026]. The 2-stock hypothesis is discussed separately below.

:::
